<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_BEGIN -->
The Maldives is one of the countries most at risk from rising sea levels due to climate change. The island nation is made up of 26 atolls and 1,190 coral islands, with an average elevation of just 1.5 meters above sea level. As a result, even a small rise in sea level could have catastrophic consequences for the Maldives.

To cope with the rising sea levels and the threat of climate change, the Maldives has undertaken a number of initiatives, including:

1. Developing renewable energy: The Maldives aims to generate 100% of its electricity from renewable sources by 2025. The government has implemented a number of initiatives to encourage the use of solar and wind power, including installing solar panels on public buildings and offering incentives for households and businesses to switch to renewable energy.

2. Protecting coral reefs: Coral reefs are crucial to the Maldives' economy and environment, providing habitat for fish and other marine life, and protecting the islands from erosion. The government has launched a number of initiatives to protect the reefs, including setting up marine parks and implementing fishing restrictions.

3. Building sea walls: The government has constructed sea walls and other barriers to protect vulnerable areas from flooding and erosion. The walls are designed to absorb the force of the waves and prevent them from reaching the shore.

4. Relocating communities: In some cases, the government has relocated communities from low-lying islands to higher ground. This has been a controversial measure, as many islanders are reluctant to leave their ancestral homes.

5. Advocating for global action: The Maldives has been an outspoken advocate for global action on climate change, calling on other countries to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions and take steps to prevent further warming of the planet.

Despite these efforts, the Maldives remains highly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. The government and international organizations continue to work on new initiatives and innovations to help mitigate the effects of rising sea levels on this fragile island nation.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_END -->
